summary: Spartanburg County lookout on steel legs, about 100 ft tall in a 1957 survey; the lookout-history site lists it as removed.

facts.design: Cabin on four structural steel legs
facts.status_note: The lookout-history site lists the tower as removed. No source read describes what remains on the hill.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey describes the station as a cabin on four steel legs, so the tower was already standing
National Geodetic Survey recovers the station, matching the 1957 description
North Carolina Geodetic Survey recovers the station as described

evidence.supports: Lookout-history site marks the tower as removed

evidence.supports: Statewide: most operators from the 1960s on were women, often married to firefighters
evidence.quote: From the 1960s on, most South Carolina tower operators were women; frequently their husbands were employed as firefighters.

corrections.why: The NGS description gives the structure as about 100 feet tall. The 10-foot figure in the same sentence is the cabin, not the height.

sources.title: NGS Data Sheet, PID FB2799 (August Hill Lookout Tower)

notes_for_editor: The record's 3.0 m height looks like a misreading of the 10-foot cabin; NGS gives about 100 feet, so 30.5 m is proposed. A 2000 goupstate.com article (seen only as a search snippet, fetch returned HTTP 403) gives August Hill as 103 feet and as one of four Spartanburg County towers; not used because it could not be read and quoted. No source read gives a build date, staffing, fires or a removal date. The 'removed' status rests on one site tag. Access and visit details are unknown and left out.
